place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 药园 · 这一年
place.en: Chending Temple · The herb garden · That year

setup.zh: 马小宝告到执事房：官丹卖了。周衡定下日子——端午辰时，正殿前，当众验封；封条动过，搜铺，搜身。你那道封条，是去年拿米汤粘回去的。
setup.en: Ma Xiaobao has gone to the stewards' office: the temple pill was sold. Zhou Heng has set the day — the Dragon Boat festival, the hour of the dragon, before the main hall, the seal inspected in public; if the seal has been touched, your bunk is searched and so are you. That seal is the one you pasted back with rice water last year.

recap.zh: 端午验封，那一角在你拇指底下翘了一翘，你焐住了；周衡记下「验封。完好。」，又问了一句孙二狗那颗丹几道纹——「我看了」。一晃五年；入秋，丹田那片湖满得往外漾——九层大圆满。
recap.en: At the Dragon Boat inspection the corner lifted under your thumb and you held it down with your own warmth; Zhou Heng wrote "Seal inspected. Intact." — and asked how many rings Sun Ergou's pill had: "I looked." Five years went by; in autumn the lake in your dantian brimmed over — layer nine, great perfection.

zh: 米汤糊的窗纸，过不了黄梅天。
en: Dragon Boat, the hour of the dragon, before the main hall: the seal.
Rice-water paste never outlasts the plum rains.
Qingming, Dragon Boat, the dog days, autumn.

story.zh:
往后残株一个月一篮，篮子一年比一年浅，两三个月才出得一颗。

马小宝去钱掌柜的摊子上一押三十两，押了七回，连一颗一道纹的也没押着。押到第七回，他不押了。他去了执事房。

「周师兄，」他当着一屋子领灵石的人道，「沈小满那颗官丹，卖了。钱掌柜这辈子，除了腊八那一文，没开过头彩，这是他自己赌咒说的。一个大比时才四层的，一开春便是五层，还一包一包的丹送人——他拿什么换的？他是拿观主赐的丹，跟钱掌柜换的。」

这话有人信。一个四层拿了宗门的头名，全观嘀咕了一冬，没人说得清他是怎么赢的；如今他又一包一包往外送丹——卖丹，倒比碰巧说得通。不到天黑，内门的饭堂里也在说这件事了。

周衡的笔停了。官丹上了他的账，丢了、卖了，都是他账上一个窟窿。他把小满叫了来，道：「官丹的封，是观主的印。要验，得拿正殿的印模来对。印模在观主手里，观主闭关，端午出关。端午辰时，正殿前，验封。」说完，又把观规念了一遍，念得跟念账一样平：「封条若是动过，是私揭官封。搜铺，搜身，交戒律堂。」当天傍晚，戒律堂便来了话：宗门头名的官丹，端午那天，戒律堂的执事亲自到。又把药园的巡夜簿要了去——观里出了事，先问挂巡夜令的。

马小宝笑了：「搜身好。」

小满也笑，笑得比他还好看，后背却一寸一寸地凉了下去。搜铺，搜的是包袱里那只小铜炉——炉盖一掀，玉盒子、两颗九转筑基丹，都在它肚里；搜身，搜的是胸口那个油纸包，贴着油纸包的那块木牌，和腰带夹层里那只赤松观的储物袋。东西从马小宝手里搜出来，头一个知道的不是戒律堂，是马家；马家的白衣仙长，当年在黑松岭出银子，要逮的就是一只银狐狸。锁儿是怎么死的，他记得。

从那天起，马小宝那几个跟班轮着班跟他：他挑水，井边便有人洗手；他上茅房，隔壁便有人蹲着；夜里，他左右两张铺，都换上了马小宝的人；戒律堂的弟子路过大通铺，也要往他铺上多看一眼。包袱他再不离身，挑水背着，睡觉枕着，小狰盘在上头。离端午，还有两个多月。

那几个月里，最难的倒不是修炼，是忍。

马小宝的人吃饭跟着，挑水跟着，茅房也跟着；他走到哪里，哪里便有一双眼睛，等着他从怀里掉出一样说不清来历的东西来。他一样也没掉，一个月下来，人瘦了一圈。
story.en:
After that the culls came one basket a month, the basket shallower every year, and a pill only every two or three months.

Ma Xiaobao went to Shopkeeper Qian's stall and staked thirty taels a time, seven times, and did not win so much as a one-ring pill. After the seventh, he stopped. He went to the stewards' office.

"Brother Zhou," he said, before a roomful of people come for their spirit stones, "Shen Xiaoman's temple pill — he sold it. Shopkeeper Qian has never paid out a top prize in his life except that one copper at Laba; he swore it himself. Layer four at the contest, layer five come spring, and packet after packet of pills to give away — what does he trade for them? He traded the pill the Abbot gave him, to Shopkeeper Qian."

People believed it. A layer-four had taken first place in the whole temple's contest, and the whole temple had muttered about it all winter — no one could say how he had won; now he was handing out pills by the packet. Selling the pill made better sense than luck. Before dark they were talking of it in the inner court's dining hall too.

Zhou Heng's brush stopped. The temple pill was on his books; lost or sold, it was a hole in his accounts. He sent for Xiaoman and said: "The seal on a temple pill is the Abbot's stamp. To check it, it must be laid against the stamp mould in the main hall. The mould is in the Abbot's hands; the Abbot is in seclusion, and comes out at the Dragon Boat festival. Dragon Boat, hour of the dragon, before the main hall: seal inspection." Then he recited the temple rule, as flat as reading out an account: "If the seal has been touched, that is breaking a temple seal. The bunk is searched, the body is searched, and the matter goes to the Hall of Discipline." That same evening word came from the Hall of Discipline: for the temple pill of the contest's first place, the Hall's own warden would come in person on the Dragon Boat festival. And the Hall sent for the herb garden's night-watch book — when anything went wrong in the temple, the one who wore the night-watch tag was asked first.

Ma Xiaobao smiled. "Searching the body — good."

Xiaoman smiled too, and smiled better than he did, while his back went cold inch by inch. Search the bunk, and they would find the little bronze furnace in his bundle — lift its lid, and the jade box and two nine-turn Foundation pills were all in its belly. Search the body, and they would find the oilpaper packet at his chest, the wooden token lying against it, and the Chisong Temple storage pouch in the hidden fold of his belt. Whatever Ma Xiaobao dug out, the first to hear of it would not be the Hall of Discipline but the Ma house; and the Ma house's Immortal in White was the one who had once paid silver in Black Pine Ridge to catch a silver fox. He remembered how Suo'er had died.

From that day Ma Xiaobao's hangers-on took turns following him: when he drew water, someone was washing his hands at the well; when he went to the latrine, someone was squatting next door; at night, the bunks on either side of him were both Ma Xiaobao's men; and the Hall of Discipline's disciples, passing the long bunk, gave his bed an extra look. He never let his bundle out of reach again: he carried it on his back to fetch water, slept with his head on it, and the little Zheng curled on top. The Dragon Boat festival was a little over two months off.

In those months the hardest thing was not the cultivating. It was the holding still.

Ma Xiaobao's men followed him to meals, to the well, even to the latrine; wherever he went a pair of eyes went too, waiting for something he couldn't account for to drop out of his coat. Nothing dropped. A month of it, and he was a size thinner.

exits.means: the spring month: burns paper for his grandfather; the rice-water corner lifts like a dog's ear; Ma's man catches him out of bed and the woodshed is watched; A-He's ash, buried under his quilt

story.zh:
清明那天，他在后山寻了一块向着蒙山的石头，替外公烧了一沓黄纸——外公的坟在镇上，他去不了。他念着他娘教的口诀，念到「五居中央」，纸烧完了，灰飞起来，打着旋儿往山下去。身后的林子里，有个跟班蹲在那里，蹲得腿都麻了。

清明过后，雨便没停过。柴房的墙根返了潮，饭桶的铜肚子上，也结了一层细细的水珠。一天夜里，等左右两边的鼾声都起了，他摸进柴房，把玉盒子掏出来，就着蜡烛一照，心便沉了：去年拿米汤粘回去的那一角，翘起来了，翘得像一只狗耳朵，翘起的地方，还长了一点灰毛。

他娘说过：米汤糊的窗纸，过不了黄梅天。

他吹了蜡烛，把盒子塞回饭桶，摸黑回到大通铺。左手那张铺是空的。那个最瘦的跟班坐在门槛上，抱着膝盖，在黑地里瞧着他，道：「茅房在外头。」

第二天早饭，马小宝端着碗从他身后走过去，脚也没停，只丢下一句：「柴房夜里冷，多穿点。」打那以后，柴房门口夜夜蹲着一个人。

那天傍晚，他去药园东角寻阿禾。

小满蹲在她旁边，问：「潮了的东西，怎么弄干，又不发黄？」

阿禾没抬头：「晾，不能烤。种子返了潮，埋进草木灰里，灰吃潮气，不吃颜色。」她又道：「埋严实。露一个角，就白埋了。」

她没问他要弄干什么。

当夜他讨了一簸箕灶灰，柴房去不得了，便蒙在被窝里，左右两边的鼾声一起一落，他摸着黑把玉盒子连封条埋进灰里，塞回饭桶肚里。炉盖合上那一声「咔哒」，他拿整个身子压着，压得没了声音。
story.en:
On Qingming he found a rock on the back hill facing Mengshan and burned a stack of yellow paper for Grandfather — Grandfather's grave was in the town, and he could not go. He recited the formula his mother had taught him; as he reached "five in the middle", the paper burned out, and the ash flew up and spun away down the mountain. In the trees behind him one of the hangers-on squatted until his legs went numb.

After Qingming the rain never stopped. The woodshed walls sweated at the foot, and even the Rice Tub's bronze belly beaded with fine drops of water. One night, when the snoring had started on both sides of him, he slipped into the woodshed, took out the jade box, held it to the candle, and his heart sank: the corner he had pasted back with rice water last year had lifted, curled up like a dog's ear, with a little grey fur of mould where it rose.

His mother used to say: window paper pasted with rice water never outlasts the plum rains.

He blew out the candle, put the box back in the Rice Tub, and felt his way back to the long bunk. The bunk on his left was empty. The thinnest of the hangers-on sat on the threshold hugging his knees, watching him in the dark, and said: "The latrine's outside."

At breakfast the next day Ma Xiaobao walked past behind him with his bowl, not even slowing, and dropped one sentence: "Cold in the woodshed at night. Wrap up." From then on someone squatted at the woodshed door every night.

That evening he went to find A-He at the east corner of the herb garden.

Xiaoman squatted beside her and asked: "Something's got damp. How do you dry it without it yellowing?"

A-He did not look up. "Air it; don't bake it. When seed gets damp you bury it in wood ash — ash eats the damp, not the colour." Then: "Bury it tight. Leave a corner showing and you've buried it for nothing."

She didn't ask what he wanted to dry.

That night he begged a dustpan of stove ash. The woodshed was closed to him now, so he did it under his quilt, the snoring rising and falling on either side, burying the jade box, seal and all, in the ash by feel and tucking it back into the Rice Tub. When the lid closed with its click, he pressed his whole body over it until there was no sound at all.

exits.means: the early-summer month: a surge in the night, and next morning his strength splits the chopping block — Ma counts down five days on his fingers; then the public seal inspection — he holds the lifting corner down with his thumb

refuse.en: One season at a time: finish the one before first.

story.zh:
端午前六天夜里，那个月开出来的一颗九转聚气丹落了肚，丹田里那口水缸「哗」地又涨了一截。他在被窝里咬着被角，气也不敢喘粗。第二天一早劈柴，他还照着昨天的手劲使，一斧头下去，那根碗口粗的柴连着底下的木墩子一齐裂成了两半。他愣了一愣，赶紧捂着手腕叫唤，说木墩子本来就有一道缝。伙房大娘瞧着那木墩子，又瞧着他，道：「这墩子我用了快二十年。」窗外头一个跟班撒腿便跑。

那天晚饭，马小宝隔着三张桌子，冲他伸出一只巴掌，五个指头，一个一个往回扳。

端午那天，下着毛毛雨。正殿前的廊下挤满了人，外门来了大半，内门也来了不少，廊下站不下，便打着伞站到雨里——宗门的头名是不是拿官丹换了钱，人人都想亲眼瞧一瞧。周衡身后站着戒律堂的执事，执事身后四个戒律堂的弟子，空着手，等着搜。殿前不许带兵器，一个戒律堂的弟子先在他腰上、袖筒里拍了一遍，又拍了一遍，从腰带上摸出一把短刀，翻过来看了看：凡铁，刀口缺了三个牙。他把刀扔回给小满。那只手，离腰带里那个夹层，只差两指。一个道童捧出印模来，周衡把玉盒子举到廊檐底下，拿印模往大印上一扣，一丝不差。

他把玉盒递还给小满：「拿稳了。」转身去翻观主的印簿，对这一颗丹是哪一天封的。

小满捧着玉盒，拇指压在那一角上。雨气从廊檐外头漫进来，他觉得拇指底下，那只狗耳朵轻轻地，又抬了一抬。他不敢动，也不敢使灵力——廊下几百双眼睛，手上冒一丝热气，便是不打自招。他只是压着，把胸口那口憋住的气细细地、长长地吐出去，拿自己手上那点热，一点一点地焐。马小宝就站在三步开外，眼睛盯着的，正是他那只拇指。

周衡合上印簿，接过玉盒，拿指甲顺着封条的四条边，一寸一寸刮过去。刮到那一角，指甲停了一停，比别处多停了一眨眼。他的眼睛在小满那只拇指上落了一落——拇指肚上压出了一道红印子。

周衡在账簿上记了一行：**验封。完好。**

马小宝的脸，青一阵，白一阵，挤出人堆走了。人散得很慢，好些人走出去老远，还回过头来瞧他：封条验得完好，一个四层怎么赢的头名，却验不出来。

封条是干净了，那一身泥却没处落，落到了钱掌柜身上。他是马小宝点了名的买主，那天也叫戒律堂传上了山，在廊角站了一早上。戒律堂的执事当场发了话：一文钱押出来的头彩，说不清；说不清的摊子，三年不许上山。钱掌柜一句没争，把算盘揣进袖子，秤杆往肩上一扛。

他走过小满跟前，站住了：「明年押不了你了。后年也押不了。」隔了一会儿，又道：「那木头，打听出名字没有？」小满摇了摇头。钱掌柜点点头，下山去了。

戒律堂的执事走在人后头。他从小满身边过，脚也没停，眼睛也没往他脸上落，只撂下一句：「下回焐东西，别用拇指。拇指的汗多。」说完，出了廊檐，进了雨里，一会儿便看不见了。

人散了，周衡却叫住小满，把账簿往胳膊底下一夹，低声问了一句：「孙二狗那颗聚气丹，几道纹？」

小满道：「他吃得急，没顾上看。」

周衡看着他，道：「我看了。」

那天回到大通铺，小满坐在铺沿上脱鞋，脱了半天没脱下来。手在抖。
story.en:
Six nights before the Dragon Boat festival, the nine-turn qi pill that month's feedings had brought out went down, and the great jar in his dantian rose with another rush. He lay biting the corner of his quilt, not daring to breathe hard. Next morning at the woodpile he swung with yesterday's strength, and one stroke split the log as thick as a bowl's mouth and the chopping block under it clean in two. He stood stunned a moment, then clutched his wrist and yelped that the block had had a crack in it all along. The kitchen aunt looked at the block, then at him: "I've used that block nearly twenty years." Outside the window a hanger-on took to his heels.

At supper that day Ma Xiaobao, three tables away, held up one hand to him, five fingers, and folded them down one by one.

On the Dragon Boat festival a fine rain was falling. The gallery before the main hall was packed: most of the outer court had come, and a good many of the inner court; those the gallery could not hold stood out in the rain under umbrellas — whether the contest's first place had sold the temple pill for money, everyone wanted to see with their own eyes. Behind Zhou Heng stood the warden of the Hall of Discipline, and behind the warden four of the Hall's disciples, empty-handed, waiting to search. No weapons were allowed before the hall; one of the Hall's disciples patted down his waist and sleeves, then patted them down again, and drew a short knife from his belt, turned it over and looked: plain iron, three nicks in the edge. He tossed it back to Xiaoman. That hand had come within two fingers of the hidden fold in his belt. A temple boy brought out the stamp mould; Zhou Heng held the jade box up under the eaves and pressed the mould onto the great seal — not a hair's difference.

He handed the jade box back to Xiaoman — "Hold it steady" — and turned to leaf through the Abbot's seal register for the day this pill had been sealed.

Xiaoman held the jade box, his thumb pressed on that corner. The damp of the rain drifted in under the eaves, and under his thumb he felt the dog's ear lift, gently, once more. He dared not move, nor use his spirit power — with hundreds of eyes under the eaves, one wisp of heat off his hand would be a confession. He only pressed, let the breath held tight in his chest out thin and long, and warmed the corner, little by little, with the warmth of his own hand. Ma Xiaobao stood three paces off, and what his eyes were fixed on was that thumb.

Zhou Heng closed the register, took the jade box, and ran his fingernail along the four edges of the seal, inch by inch. At that corner the nail paused — one blink longer than anywhere else. His eyes rested a moment on Xiaoman's thumb: a red mark pressed into the pad of it.

Zhou Heng wrote a line in the ledger: **Seal inspected. Intact.**

Ma Xiaobao's face went green, then white, and he pushed out through the crowd. The people went slowly, and many, a long way off, still turned back to look at him: the seal had checked out whole, but how a layer-four had won first place — no seal could check that.

The seal was clean; but the mud had to land somewhere, and it landed on Shopkeeper Qian. He was the buyer Ma Xiaobao had named, and the Hall of Discipline had summoned him up the mountain that day too; he had stood all morning at the corner of the gallery. The Hall's warden gave his word on the spot: a top prize won on a single copper could not be accounted for, and a stall that could not be accounted for would not come up the mountain for three years. Shopkeeper Qian did not argue a word. He tucked his abacus into his sleeve and shouldered his steelyard.

Passing Xiaoman, he stopped. "Can't bet on you next year. Nor the year after." A pause; then: "That wood — found out its name yet?" Xiaoman shook his head. Shopkeeper Qian nodded and went down the mountain.

The warden of the Hall of Discipline went last. He passed Xiaoman without breaking step, without letting his eyes fall on his face, and dropped one sentence: "Next time you warm something, don't use your thumb. A thumb sweats." Then he was out from under the eaves and into the rain, and in a moment he could not be seen.

When the people had gone, Zhou Heng called Xiaoman back, tucked the ledger under his arm, and asked, low: "Sun Ergou's qi pill — how many rings?"

Xiaoman said: "He ate it in a hurry. Didn't stop to look."

Zhou Heng looked at him and said: "I looked."

Back at the long bunk that day, Xiaoman sat on the edge of it to take off his shoes, and could not get them off for a long while. His hands were shaking.

label.en: The dog days · Five years go by

exits.means: the hot month: nights on the herb-garden wall with A-He and Sun Ergou — then five years in a few lines (layers six to nine; no going home before Foundation; five brides on the Zhang)

refuse.en: One season at a time: finish the one before first.

story.zh:
端午一过，跟班们便撤了。

伏天里最热的那几夜，药园巡完了，三个人常坐在药园的矮墙上乘凉：小满，阿禾，孙二狗。

小满问：「你想叫什么？」孙二狗想了半天，道：「……还叫二狗吧。我娘叫惯了。」

小满没笑。阿禾也没笑。墙底下的小狰翻了个身，打了个响鼻。

一晃，便是五年。

看官，凡人修仙，最不值钱的是日子。练气头几层，几个月一层；越往上越慢，一层爬上一两年，是常事；从练气到筑基，十年八年算快的，一辈子爬不上去的，十个里倒有九个。小满的外公，当年拿七年练到九层大圆满，在沉鼎观已算得快了。

沈小满这五年，说书的只消几行。他一年一层：六层，七层，八层，九层；七层上卡了大半年，他也不急。秘境里那一撮土，在他丹田里长成了一块厚地，吸一口，存一口，一滴不漏；残株一年比一年少，饭桶两三个月才吐一颗九道纹的，他吃一颗，那口缸便深一截。夜里他坐着吐纳，木牌贴在心口，凉的时候多，暖的时候少；可他知道，他睡着以后，有一只爪子还在他身子里，一下一下地凿。

五年里，他一回也没回过石坳村。瞿老不许：「没筑基，别下山。」又道：「在你家门口站过一夜的那个人，等的就是你下山。」家信一年两封，他娘的字仍旧又小又密：屋顶不漏了；你爹的膝盖，阴天疼，晴天也疼；吴婆婆的牙，还在。

内门的屋子，一间也没空出来——内门的人筑不了基，又不肯下山，屋子便不空。他仍旧睡在大通铺最靠门的那张铺上，巡夜令挂在腰里，园里一株也没少过。大比年年比，那一颗筑基丹，年年是内门的；他再没上过五行台——怀里已揣着一颗，不去抢第二颗。秦雁第二年进了内门，第五年上，筑了基。孙二狗一年一层，爬到了三层，爬上一层，便在大通铺门口哭一回。阿禾那一尺地年年种，年年多半是瘪穗；她的修为跟着那几棵禾，一年只挪一点。钱掌柜那三年的禁，到第四年端午满了，他把板子又扛上了山，见了小满，头一句话是：「那木头，打听出名字没有？」

每年除夕，周衡都要去一趟正殿；每年从正殿出来，都说一句：「明年，弟子再来。」观主每年都是那一句：外门里，今年没人筑基。每年十月十八，周衡一整天不翻账簿，巡夜的蜡烛，也不掰了。小满不问。

这五年，漳水边上，每年十月十八，推下去一只船，船上坐一个穿嫁衣的姑娘。五年，五只船。沉鼎观离漳水十天的路，观里没有一个人知道她们叫什么。周衡知道是哪一天。
story.en:
Once the Dragon Boat festival was past, the hangers-on were called off.

On the hottest nights of the dog days, when the garden round was done, the three of them would sit on the herb garden's low wall to cool off: Xiaoman, A-He, Sun Ergou.

Xiaoman asked: "What would you like to be called?" Sun Ergou thought for a long time and said: "…Ergou still. My mother's used to it."

Xiaoman did not laugh. Nor did A-He. Under the wall the little Zheng rolled over and snorted.

Five years went by in a blink.

Reader, in mortal cultivation days are the cheapest thing there is. The first few layers of Qi Refining take a few months each; the higher you climb the slower it goes, a year or two for a single layer is common; from Qi Refining to Foundation, eight or ten years counts as fast, and nine in ten never make it in a lifetime. Xiaoman's grandfather had taken seven years to reach layer nine, great perfection, and at Chending Temple that already counted as quick.

Shen Xiaoman's five years the storyteller can tell in a few lines. One layer a year: six, seven, eight, nine; he was stuck at seven for most of a year and did not fret. The pinch of earth from the secret realm had grown into a field of thick soil in his dantian: one breath in, one breath kept, not a drop leaking. The culls dwindled year by year, the Rice Tub gave up a nine-ring pill only every two or three months, and each one he ate made the jar a little deeper. At night he sat breathing, the token against his heart, cool more often than warm; but he knew that once he slept, a claw was still at work inside him, chipping, stroke by stroke.

In five years he never once went back to Shi'ao Village. Old Qu would not allow it: "No Foundation, no going down the mountain." And: "The man who stood a night at your door is waiting for exactly that." Letters came twice a year, his mother's hand still small and dense: the roof doesn't leak now; your father's knee hurts when it's overcast, and when it's clear too; Granny Wu's teeth are still there.

Not one inner-court room came free — inner-court people who couldn't lay their Foundation wouldn't go down the mountain either, so the rooms never emptied. He still slept in the bunk nearest the door, the night-watch token at his belt, and not one plant went missing from the garden. The contest came round every year, and every year the one Foundation pill went to the inner court; he never set foot on the Five Elements Stage again — with one already in his coat, he didn't go after a second. Qin Yan entered the inner court the next year, and in the fifth year she laid her Foundation. Sun Ergou climbed a layer a year, up to three, and every layer he climbed he cried once at the door of the long bunk. A-He sowed her foot of earth every year, and every year most of the ears were empty; her cultivation followed those few stalks, moving only a little each year. Shopkeeper Qian's three-year ban ran out at the Dragon Boat festival of the fourth year, and he carried his board up the mountain again; the first thing he said when he saw Xiaoman was: "That wood — found out its name yet?"

Every New Year's Eve, Zhou Heng went to the main hall; every year he came out and said, "Next year I'll come again." Every year the abbot said the same thing: nobody in the outer court has laid a Foundation this year. Every year on the eighteenth of the tenth month Zhou Heng did not open his ledger all day, and did not break his night-watch candle in half. Xiaoman did not ask.

In those five years, every eighteenth of the tenth month, a boat was pushed out on the Zhang with a girl in a bridal gown sitting in it. Five years, five boats. Chending Temple was ten days from the Zhang, and no one in it knew their names. Zhou Heng knew which day it was.

exits.means: the autumn month: the lake brims over, layer nine, great perfection; his master calls him up the cliff

refuse.zh: 一季一季来：先过了前头那一季。
refuse.en: One season at a time: finish the one before first.

story.zh:
到得入秋，丹田里那口水缸满得往外直漾，吸进去一口灵气，便溢出来一口，再也添不进去了——外门的人管这个叫「九层巅峰」；褚先生的名册上，只写四个字：九层大圆满。

八月里，瞿老叫他上了一趟崖顶。
story.en:
By autumn the great jar in his dantian was brimming over: breathe in one breath of spirit and one spilled out; nothing more would go in — the outer court called this "the peak of layer nine"; in Master Chu's register it was written in four characters only: layer nine, great perfection.

In the eighth month, Old Qu called him up to the clifftop.
